subject: Offer: goodwill package after inference outage (Gridly)
messages:
From: Aisha Shah <aisha@gridly.io>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Riley <tom.riley@gridly.io>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 503s and inference errors across prod - urgent

Hi Kimberly,

We're seeing a spike in 503s and corrupted responses from the Redwood API between ~07:40 and 09:00 PT this morning. Our product is failing health checks and rolling back workers; it's impacted ~12% of requests across our EU and US fleets. Our SREs attached a brief log sample and a timeline (gridly_incident_logs.zip).

Can you confirm whether this was a platform-level regression or a configuration issue on our side? Given the customer impact, we'll need a remediation plan and an estimate on credits while we investigate.

What's most helpful now: a short incident summary, ETA for root cause, and any immediate mitigation steps we should apply.

Thanks —
Aisha
Sr. Product Ops, Gridly

Attachment: gridly_incident_logs.zip (ZIP, 1.2 MB)
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Aisha Shah <aisha@gridly.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 503s and inference errors across prod - urgent

Hi Aisha —

I'm very sorry you're hitting this. We saw correlated error spikes in our telemetry and have an active incident running; engineering is on the remediation path now. Initial notes:
- We identified a queuing regression in the batching layer that caused KV cache churn at higher tail latencies.
- Mitigation: routing a percentage of traffic to an older batching policy should reduce 503s within ~30–45 minutes.

We absolutely want to make this right for Gridly. Once we have a short postmortem, I'm prepared to offer a goodwill package (credits + a 30–60 day trial extension). Before I propose specifics, can you confirm which HubSpot deal to tie credits to? Also attaching an empty placeholder offer PDF for internal review.

I'll loop Ben for approvals on the numbers. We'll follow up with a formal offer and a DocuSign link.

—Kimberly
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachment: compensation_offer.pdf (PDF, stub)
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Intermittent 503s and inference errors across prod - urgent

Ben / Markus — forwarding Gridly's incident. TL;DR: production 503s impacting ~12% of requests across regions. Customer asks for remediation summary + credits.

Proposed offer: $5,000 service credit applied to their account + 45-day trial extension on dedicated features (priority routing + 24/7 support) — OR alternatively a token credit equivalent (approx. 2M tokens). I think a combined smaller dollar credit + extended trial is better for retention.

Please reply with: approved yes/no, and any changes to amount or term.

Quoted message below.

Also: flag support to monitor Gridly's traffic for the next 14 days (priority watch). After the postmortem, include a concrete rollback/fix timeline and any code-level mitigation notes.

Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Goodwill package and next steps — Gridly (DEAL-9832)

Hi Aisha / Tom —

Thanks again for raising this and apologies for the disruption. Per our investigation and leadership approval, here's the offer we've prepared:

1) $5,000 account credit to be applied to DEAL-9832 in HubSpot.
2) 45-day trial extension for access to priority routing and 24/7 support.
3) One month of priority monitoring by our SRE team (we'll mute lower-priority alerts and proactively advise on traffic shaping).

I've attached the official offer PDF (compensation_offer.pdf) and included a DocuSign link to accept the terms: https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/tx/ABCDEF123456

We'll also follow up with a short postmortem within 72 hours summarizing the root cause (batching layer regression) and the permanent fix timeline. Once the DocuSign is signed, Ben will schedule the priority monitoring handoff and Support will apply the credit.

Let me know if you'd prefer token credit instead of dollar credit — we can convert $5k to ~2M tokens.

Sincerely,
Kimberly Park
